### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c573f09f9f6acdee64a6075f73de88792b40fc7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `15c1048a6713cf6fc0b5fffd8420f3d8ebc423b8`

### ① Derived judgments

Measured on the diff `588475c30..15c1048a6` (merge base with `origin/main` at review time `00115a844`): 3 files, `packages/client/src/index.ts` +65/−11 in three hunks (the `invite` docblock and body, the `resend` docblock, the `resend` body), one new test file, one changeset. No `packages/spec/**`, no `*.zod.ts`, no error-code ledger, no `packages/spec/api-surface/*` row is touched. `check-widening-tells` reports all 3 files NOT MEASURED — no declared surface covers `packages/client/src/**` — so the tells are blind on this diff and the judgments below are the whole gate.

1. **`organizations.invite` request type gains `teamId?: string | null`** (the declared widening). Real, and reachable: `ObjectStackClient` is the package's exported class, the parameter type is inline on the public property, `dist/index.d.ts` is emitted from this source (`files: [dist, …]`, `check-dts-emitted`), and the new suite's ⑤ pins `Parameters` of it at exactly `string | null | undefined`. The PR declares this as the widening and it is the only published TYPE that widens — right. Also right on the merits: at the merge base `invite` already forwarded every extra member through `{ ...req }`, so a string `teamId` already reached the wire undeclared; the declaration turns an enforced-but-undeclared member into a declared one (the mirror of the card's declared-but-unenforced defect), and `invite` is `resend`'s only route to the wire.
2. **`invite` runtime accept set: `teamId: null` now collapses to absence** (200, no team) where the merge-base spread would have put `"teamId":null` on the wire and the vendor answers 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`. This is a runtime widening the declaration does not name (it was unreachable for an object-literal caller but reachable structurally). Right: `null` is this SDK's own read-back spelling (`OrganizationInvitationWire.teamId: string | null`, `invitations.list`), `resend` has declared `string | null` since `371445c27`, and a verbatim forward would have converted the silent drop into a loud 400 on every `list()` round trip (pinned by ③, ④b, ④f; ablation leg B red).
3. **`invite` body byte order: `teamId` now serialises last** regardless of caller position (④e); every other member keeps its position and an omitted/null `teamId` is byte-identical to the pre-#17274 body (④c, sibling #16582 pins unchanged in the diff). JSON member order is not wire semantics — right.
4. **`organizations.invitations.resend` type is unchanged** (`teamId?: string | null` stays; direction 2 was not taken) and its runtime now forwards the member. That is delivery of an already-declared member — 拉回已声明契约, not a widening and not a narrowing of the published type — right, and it is the repair triage's grading mandated (补实现或退役, never a consumer-side narrowing).
5. **A refusal now fires where it did not**: `resend` with a non-existent `teamId` used to resolve 200 (the id never left the SDK) and now rejects with the vendor's 400 `TEAM_NOT_FOUND` through the existing generic `fetch` error path (case ②). The PR body's "Nothing is narrowed" is true of the compile-time accept set and of every call that ever worked as declared, but not of that runtime path; I name it as a separate judgment the declaration does not cover. Judged right: the published type promised a placement, a placement that cannot exist is exactly what the declared contract must refuse, the refusal is the vendor's own and the SDK adds no guard, and the card and triage both asked for the silent success to become loud. Not a clause-② narrowing in the SKILL sense (it enforces the declared contract), and not the runtime permission/security floor (no authorization behaviour moves).
6. **Error-code surface: no new code.** `TEAM_NOT_FOUND` is stamped nowhere in non-test source by this diff (docblock mention and a test that constructs it, which the provenance gate's own rule says is not a producer); it is a better-auth organization-plugin pass-through in the same unregistered class as `ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` / `INVITATION_NOT_FOUND` / `ROLE_NOT_FOUND` (none in `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`), and it was already reachable through the published surface at the merge base via `invite`'s spread and the `teams.*` methods. No ledger entry is owed by this PR — right. Whether that vendor class should be ledgered at all is a pre-existing spec-lane question, recorded in ③, not a defect of this diff.
7. **`resend` drops its own `role ?? 'member'` and takes `invite`'s default.** Read at the tree: `rest` carries `role: undefined` in position 2 and the reassignment keeps that position, so bytes are identical on every path (④c, ④d) — behaviour-neutral, right; the `invite` docblock sentence it falsified is corrected in the same hunk — right.
8. **The new test file exports `resendTeamIdStaysDeclared17274`.** Not a published export: `tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts` from the build program and `files` ships `dist` only; same pattern as the sibling's `inviteRoleStaysOptional16582` — right.
9. **JSDoc on `invite` and `resend`** ships in the `.d.ts` as documentation of the measured vendor behaviour; no contract claim in it contradicts the diff — right.
10. **Nothing else widens.** No new exported symbol, no new key elsewhere, no schema arm, no registry row, no changed refusal beyond item 5. The declared widening is real and it is the whole of the TYPE widening; items 2 and 5 are the runtime deltas the one-line declaration does not spell out, both judged right above.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/17274-invitations-resend-team-placement.md` grades `@objectstack/client: minor`. Consistent with the diff: an additive optional member on a published request type is `minor`, and the repo's own level axis requires it — `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main --head 15c1048a6 --event (PR payload)` on `origin/main` scripts exits 0: no `major`, direction arm read as `widening`, and no package whose `packages/**/src/**` moves is graded `patch`. `check-adr-0087-registration` exits 0 (one non-breaking changeset; no disposition marker owed — nothing is removed or renamed). Precedent on the same file: the #14314 type-surface change shipped `minor` under the lockstep no-major convention. The changeset's text matches the diff on every claim I could measure: it names the `invite` widening, the null-to-absence collapse, the `role` tidy-up, and the byte-identity of existing calls (verified by reading the body construction and by the sibling pins standing unchanged). `packages/client/CHANGELOG.md` and `content/docs/releases/` are correctly untouched (release-owned).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev `open_questions`: none raised.** Every dev-side flag answered below.
- **Carrier reading (dev reported `--pair 18429` exit 4 / C3 at hand-off):** repaired by the seat; re-read this round from `origin/main` scripts — `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 18429` exit 0, declaration readable in the fixed spelling, `needs:contract-review` on both card #17274 and PR #18429.
- **Pre-existing red `check:cross-package-test-inputs` (#18353 / #18348):** not a contract matter and not this diff's paths. Landing check ③ at this head: 38 check runs on `15c1048a6`, 32 success, 6 skipped, 0 failed — Test Core 6/6, Check Changeset, all Type Check gates green.
- **Out-of-scope 1 — vendor accepts `teamId` as a string ARRAY:** agree, not this PR's. Declaring the array form would be a further widening of a published request type — its own card and `Clause-②: yes` when it comes.
- **Out-of-scope 2 — vendor accepts `teamId: ''` with 200 and skips `TEAM_NOT_FOUND`:** agree, vendor-side; the SDK forwards `''` unchanged (the `== null` test does not catch it), which is the correct non-invention.
- **Out-of-scope 3 — better-auth's `resend?: boolean` flag vs. cancel-then-invite:** agree, deliberate and untouched.
- **Out-of-scope 4 — request-member fidelity across the 19 `organizations.*` methods has no binding artifact:** agree it is a coverage observation, not a filable class; carried by the seat with the dev's dedupe words (`organizations request member binding`, `invite-member body schema parity`, `route ledger request schema`).
- **Card open question — one member or a class #14314 missed?** Verified at the tree: `371445c27` (2026-05-07, the commit that created the `organizations.*` surface) added `teamId?: string | null` to `resend`; `7092d63e4` (#14314 / PR #16576, 2026-09-07) touched this file on the RESPONSE axis only — its own changeset text, now in `packages/client/CHANGELOG.md` 17.4.0, says "No request bytes, no URL and no response handling change" and names `resend` as unchanged. One member; #14314 could not have caught it. Answered.
- **Card's flag that only direction 2 is clause-② ("unlike direction 1"):** corrected. Direction 1 as implemented widens `invite`'s published request type, so it is `yes` too; the conservative `yes` on the claim was the right declaration and the review obligation was owed either way.
- **Negative boundary:** no runtime permission or security behaviour moves — the vendor's own authorization on `invite-member` is untouched and the SDK adds no guard. Not the security/permission floor.
- **Reviewer's own notes, none blocking:** (a) the PR body's "Nothing is narrowed" should be read as a statement about the type and about calls that ever worked as declared — see ①.5. (b) `TEAM_NOT_FOUND` and its better-auth organization-plugin siblings are not in the error-code ledger; pre-existing, not created by this diff, a spec-lane question if anyone wants the vendor pass-through class ledgered (dedupe words: `better-auth organization pass-through codes ledger`, `TEAM_NOT_FOUND ledger`). (c) The suite was read in full at the tree but not executed locally (no `node_modules` in this checkout); CI Test Core at this head is the execution of record. (d) No hand-written docs page enumerates `invite`'s request members (grep at head finds only permission-reach mentions of the route), and the docs-drift check listed nothing.

Reviewed-by: `session_01DvvamiacK328idtBYJBxV3`

**VERDICT: PASS**
